paragraphs.text: The Coreness kit for DeepSeek Harness — a plugin bundle for a profile.
# Coreness for DeepSeek Harness
Coreness is the product for one DeepSeek Harness profile: a panel in the application's sidebar, whos
e rail holds the sections for its General page, the profile's MCP servers, its Qoder provider, its r
ate limits and usage.
## Install
*Plugins* → *Add plugin*, in the application's own window, takes the package into the profile the ap
plication is running — no profile to name — and the address is:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The install lands in the running profile, and a restart is asked for only where the application cann
ot apply the change in place. Nothing is built on the way in: the package is plain files, and its ma
nifest declares no Harness version bound. The address is a git repository, so the install reads it w
ith git — a machine without git cannot install it.
By command line, and updates through the market
`dsh` is the application's own command and not one Windows or macOS comes with: the application puts
it on the path from its own menu — **Application → Manage dsh Command…** in the window's title bar
on Windows, the same item in the application menu on macOS — and a terminal opened before that act k
eeps the path it started with. The line then runs as it stands: the desktop application's own profil
e is `desktop`; another profile is named instead — the web surface's is `web` — and a name that does
not stand yet is created:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Updates go through the application's **Discover** tab: switch *Custom plugin indexes* on once (**Plu
gins → More**; an older build labels the same switch *Custom plugin markets*), add `https://raw.gith
ubusercontent.com/Vensus137/Coreness-DSH/main/market.json`, and the plugin stands listed with its ve
rsions, compared by the application itself: a newer one shows as *Update available*, whose press ope
ns the installed plugin's page. Where the application's plugin manager offers an update, that page c
arries the press: the installed version is replaced with the chosen one and kept, or installed again
, when the installation fails; where it offers none, the update is taking the plugin off and adding
it again with the same address, and *Add plugin* over the installed copy is refused. Nothing checks
in the background; the address follows the newest release, and a fixed one is named by its tag, `git
hub:Vensus137/Coreness-DSH#<tag>`.
## What a profile gets
- **The MCP servers, seen and edited** — one card per server: its kind, its address, the environment
it needs, and switches whose effect lands in the profile rather than in a copy. A server behind OAu
th is signed in from its card.
- **The Qoder models** — the account's own, each with the reasoning levels it accepts and the output
budget it allows; the token is entered once, in the Qoder section, and kept by the platform's own s

tore.
- **A limiter that waits instead of refusing** — a call over a declared limit takes its turn i
n a queue; nothing is limited until a limit is declared.
- **The Agent team, on the General page** — how many teammates a session may hold, written through t
he platform's own editor, and two switches that put the product's paragraph in place of the platform
's last team-policy sentence and add the review paragraph after it; the team is the platform's, and
every other line stays as it wrote it.
- **The page fetch and its proxy, on the General page** — *Use the improved page fetch* sends page f
etches through the product's own provider: the platform's HTTP fetch with a browser identity and a w
ider body. *Proxy for page fetch* sends a fetch through the HTTP proxy once the proxy answers a quic
k reachability check: a proxy that fails the check leaves the fetch direct, while one that fails dur
ing the fetch is reported as the error, not retried; a call left with no time for the check runs thr
ough the stored proxy unchecked — unless the whole traffic is on. *Proxy all traffic* sends every re
quest the harness itself makes — the model, search, page fetch, MCP connections and the market — thr
ough the same proxy at once, while the app's own pages, its built-in browser included, stay outside
it. All three stand off by default; the URL is kept by the platform's credential store, shown back i
n the card's field, and checked from the card.
- **The rules of the tree, in force** — the conventions the product's own tree works by, as one prom
pt section in the platform's registry: every request of the profile carries them, and no compaction
can take them out of the model's sight.
## What lands
The repository is the bundle: behind it stand the packages it names — the panel, the rules, MCP, the
OAuth sign-in, the Qoder route, the rate limiter, the team card, the page fetch and its proxy — eac
h its own plugin, so a profile switches off the ones it does not use on the application's own Plugin
s page. Nothing is fetched from the product's side; what the page shows is read from the profile and
the account it names.
